hints: For particle $B$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$, downslope forces are the 2.5 N applied force and gravity component $0.4g\sin 25^\circ$, opposed by tension $T$.
Write Newton's second law for $B$: $2.5 + 0.4g\sin 25^\circ - T = 0.4a$.
For particle $A$ of mass $0.9\text{ kg}$ on the smooth $15^\circ$ slope, tension pulls it up, opposed by downslope weight: $T - 0.9g\sin 15^\circ = 0.9a$.
Add both equations to eliminate $T$: $2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - 9\sin 15^\circ = 1.3a$, and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Write the equation of motion using Newton's second law for particle $B$ (mass $0.4\text{ kg}$) accelerating down its smooth $25^\circ$ incline:
$$2.5 + 0.4g\sin 25^\circ - T = 0.4a \implies 2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - T = 0.4a$$

Write the equation of motion for particle $A$ (mass $0.9\text{ kg}$) accelerating up its smooth $15^\circ$ incline:
$$T - 0.9g\sin 15^\circ = 0.9a \implies T - 9\sin 15^\circ = 0.9a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate string tension $T$:
$$(2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - T) + (T - 9\sin 15^\circ) = 0.4a + 0.9a$$
$$2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - 9\sin 15^\circ = 1.3a$$
teacher_walkthrough: State Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ along the lines of greatest slope for both particles connected by the taut string.

For particle $B$ on the $25^\circ$ plane moving downwards:
- Applied force: $2.5\text{ N}$ down the slope.
- Component of weight: $m_B g\sin 25^\circ = 0.4 \times 10 \times \sin 25^\circ = 4\sin 25^\circ\text{ N}$ down the slope.
- Tension $T$ acts up the slope.
$$2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - T = 0.4a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

For particle $A$ on the $15^\circ$ plane moving upwards:
- Tension $T$ pulls up the slope.
- Component of weight: $m_A g\sin 15^\circ = 0.9 \times 10 \times \sin 15^\circ = 9\sin 15^\circ\text{ N}$ down the slope.
$$T - 9\sin 15^\circ = 0.9a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate the internal tension $T$:
$$(2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - T) + (T - 9\sin 15^\circ) = 0.4a + 0.9a$$
$$2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - 9\sin 15^\circ = 1.3a$$

Divide by $1.3$ to find the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{1.86110}{1.3} \approx 1.43162\text{ m s}^{-2} = 1.43\text{ m s}^{-2} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Sets up $2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - T = 0.4a$ and $T - 9\sin 15^\circ = 0.9a$, adds to get $1.3a = 1.86\dots$, and solves for $a = 1.43\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

hints: For particle $B$, impending motion is down its $25^\circ$ slope, so limiting friction acts up the slope: $F = \mu R_B = 0.8(0.4g\cos 25^\circ) = 3.2\cos 25^\circ$.
Balance forces along the slope for $B$ in limiting equilibrium: $2.5 + 0.4g\sin 25^\circ - T - F = 0$.
For smooth particle $A$, equilibrium along its $\theta^\circ$ slope requires $T = 0.9g\sin\theta = 9\sin\theta$, and solve for $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the limiting friction force $F$ on particle $B$ (mass $0.4\text{ kg}$) on the rough $25^\circ$ plane with $\mu = 0.8$, noting friction opposes downward motion by acting up the slope:
$$R_B = 0.4g\cos 25^\circ = 4\cos 25^\circ$$
$$F = \mu R_B = 0.8(4\cos 25^\circ) = 3.2\cos 25^\circ \approx 2.9002\text{ N}$$

Set up the equilibrium equation along the slope for particle $B$:
$$2.5 + 0.4g\sin 25^\circ - T - F = 0$$
$$T = 2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - 3.2\cos 25^\circ$$
$$T \approx 2.5 + 1.69047 - 2.90018 = 1.29029\text{ N}$$

Set up the equilibrium equation along the smooth incline for particle $A$ of mass $0.9\text{ kg}$:
$$T - 0.9g\sin\theta = 0 \implies 9\sin\theta = T$$
$$9\sin\theta = 1.29029 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{1.29029}{9} \approx 0.143366$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze particle $B$ on the rough incline. With impending motion down the slope in the direction of the $2.5\text{ N}$ force, limiting friction acts up the slope:
$$R_B = m_B g\cos 25^\circ = 0.4 \times 10 \times \cos 25^\circ = 4\cos 25^\circ\text{ N}$$
$$F = \mu R_B = 0.8 \times 4\cos 25^\circ = 3.2\cos 25^\circ\text{ N}$$

Write the equilibrium condition along the plane for particle $B$:
$$2.5 + m_B g\sin 25^\circ - T - F = 0$$
$$T = 2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - 3.2\cos 25^\circ$$

Analyze particle $A$ on its smooth inclined plane: the only forces parallel to the plane are tension $T$ pulling upwards and the downslope weight component pulling downwards:
$$T - m_A g\sin\theta = 0$$
$$T = 0.9 \times 10 \times \sin\theta = 9\sin\theta$$

Equate the two expressions for tension $T$:
$$9\sin\theta = 1.29028$$

Take the inverse sine to determine $\theta$:
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.143364) \approx 8.243^\circ = 8.2^\circ \text{ (to 1 d.p.)}$$

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Calculates friction $F = 3.2\cos 25^\circ$, finds tension $T = 2.5 + 4\sin 25^\circ - 3.2\cos 25^\circ \approx 1.29\text{ N}$, equates to $9\sin\theta$, and finds $\theta = 8.2^\circ$.
